Photograph: Jono Searle/AAP View image in fullscreen The latest housing loan data shows investment in existing Australian housing is dropping in favour of new buildings. Photograph: Jono Searle/AAP Housing Lending to property investors falls sharply in ‘tiny’ step towards fairer housing market in Australia, expert says ABS data shows an almost 9% slump in new lending to investors after three interest rate hikes this year Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Cait Kelly Fri 14 Aug 2026 04.03 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google In what one economist is describing as a “tiny step” toward a fairer housing market after decades of bad policy, property investors are shying away from established homes, and putting money into new builds instead, new data shows. New lending to property investors fell sharply in the three months to June, slumping almost 9%, ABS data showed, while the number of total new home loans dropped by 5.4% in the June quarter. The major banks have all reported a slump in mortgage applications in recent months, after three RBA official rate hikes and the federal budget’s investor tax changes that together have weighed on property prices . Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email The ABS’s head of finance statistics, Mish Tan, said: “lending fell across all borrower types this quarter and returned to similar levels to this time last year”. Investor loans led the decline, falling by 8.6% in the June quarter after a 4.7% drop in the previous period. The number of investor loans was 2.8% higher than a year earlier, while the value of loans to investors was down by 10.2%. The number of loans to first home buyers dropped by 2.9% over the three-month period, to be flat over the year. Saul Eslake, a leading housing economist said the interest rates increases this year would be reducing the number of first home buyers.. Australia’s falling house prices have a silver lining for mortgage holders. Here’s why Read more “I don’t think it’s a cause for concern,” he said. “Whereas I would say the big fall in lending to investors for the purchase of established homes is actually something to be welcomed and celebrated. “Because it means that prospective first home buyers are facing less competition from investors motivated by tax breaks for the housing we’ve already got.” The number of loans to investors in established properties was down 14.8%, but the number of loans to investors buying new builds was up by 4.4% to a record high, a possible effect of the government’s budget carve-out for investor lending to build new housing. Eslake said more investment in new builds actually increased rental supply, rather than pitting renters against investors for established housing. He said these stats were a “tiny step” in the right direction to make Australia’s housing market more equal. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion Isn’t it amazing what a policy that actually tackles the cause of outrageous house prices can do? | Grogonomics Read more “A tiny step. But at least it is in that direction, whereas we’ve been taking tens of thousands of steps in the wrong direction for the last thirty years.” National spokesperson for Everybody’s Home, Maiy Azize, said the figures show the governments tax reforms were “beginning to rebalance the market”. “The most encouraging sign is that investors are pulling back from existing homes while investment in new housing is growing. That means less competition for first home buyers trying to buy a home,” Azize said. “It also smashes the myth that immigration is the main driver of house prices. When governments change the rules and stop boosting investors, housing costs go down. “Housing becoming more affordable is a good thing, especially for people trying to buy their first home.” Explore more on these topics Housing Interest rates Australian economy Banking news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Morrison-era GST deal with WA a multi-billion dollar mistake that should be reversed, Productivity Commission finds Is Australia’s buy now, pay later boom at an end? https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/.text: It could be one of the most significant resource discoveries in Poland’s history: about six kilometres from the Polish port city Świnoujście, and thus within sight of the German holiday island of Usedom, lies the Wolin East oilfield.Initial estimates suggest the newly discovered field contains around 22 million tonnes of crude oil and some five billion cubic metres of commercially recoverable natural gas.The discovery stems from exploratory drilling carried out by Canadian company Central European Petroleum (CEP) in July last year at a depth of more than 2,500 metres.'Historic moment'The Canadian company’s chief executive, Rolf G. Skaar, has described the discovery of Wolin East as a "historic moment" for the company and for Poland’s energy sector.The find has also been seen in Poland as a major opportunity for domestic energy supplies. According to Poland’s chief geologist, Krzysztof Galos, speaking in July 2025, regular production could begin in 2028 or 2029 at the earliest.Over several years, the deposit could cover around four to five percent of Poland’s annual oil demand. Wolin East could therefore make an important contribution to reducing Poland’s dependence on energy imports and strengthening the country’s security of supply.In Świnoujście, however, concern is growing about tourism and the environment: authorities and residents are insisting that the region’s appeal be preserved and nature protected.German campaign alliance against oil extraction in the Baltic SeaThe prospect of extracting fossil fuels is meeting particularly strong resistance from Germany. The non-governmental organisation BUND (German Federation for the Environment and Nature Conservation) in the state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania has joined forces with environmental group Deutsche Umwelthilfe (DUH), WWF and the citizens’ initiative Lebensraum Vorpommern in an alliance calling for a general ban on new oil and gas projects in the Baltic Sea.According to the organisers, some 88,000 signatures had been collected by the end of July this year. The petition is due to be submitted to the European Commission in Brussels in September.The organisations warn of potential damage to the Baltic’s fragile ecosystem, including underwater noise, pollutant discharges and the risk of an oil spill in protected marine areas.State election outcome could influence conflictDUH’s federal managing director, Sascha Müller-Kraenner, is calling for joint action by the federal government, the state and the EU to protect the Bay of Pomerania and the Baltic Sea as a whole:"So far, the exploratory well has not led to an authorised production project, and that must remain the case. The federal government, the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state government and the European Union must jointly send a clear message: there must be no new oil and gas extraction directly off Usedom.Just weeks before the state election, the political parties in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania must also take a clear position and explain how they intend to protect the coast from a new fossil industrial project."The upcoming state election could play a decisive role in shaping how the conflict develops between Poland’s energy interests and German environmental organisations’ calls for stronger protection for the Baltic Sea.

Photograph: REUTERS US news US schools and police warn about viral ‘Cat in the Hat’ trend after teens’ arrests Disturbing and AI-generated versions of Dr Seuss character have been used to threaten schools and communities Keely Aouga Sun 13 Sep 2026 15.15 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Schools and law enforcement authorities in the US are issuing warnings against a viral “Cat in the Hat” social media trend in which disturbing or AI-generated versions of the Dr Seuss character are used to threaten students, schools and communities. The latest warnings come as safety concerns increase and several teenagers have been arrested or charged over posts connected to the trend. The Cat in the Hat trend originated on Snapchat as images or short videos showing a disturbing version of the Cat in the Hat, often resembling the character played by Mike Myers in the 2003 live-action film, lurking outside homes, schools or on streets at night. Some footage appears to be AI-generated, while other posts include real people wearing costumes. Additionally, some videos include threatening messages towards specific towns or schools. More disturbing versions named individuals or included lists of supposed targets. The posts originally circulated in Ireland and the United Kingdom in August 2026 before quickly becoming viral in parts of the United States and Canada, the BBC reported . Even though social media users view the trend as a hoax or prank, authorities are warning that causing people to fear for their safety could potentially constitute as criminal harassment. Recently, near Wichita, Kansas , a 15-year-old was arrested after allegedly posting a video on social media that made ominous threats toward students using the trend. More than 400 people arrested at Fourth of July ‘TikTok takeover’ in California Read more A statement shared by the Hutchinson police department said that during the investigation, officers determined that a 15-year-old Hutchinson high school student created a TikTok account for that community referencing the Cat in the Hat trend. The juvenile was ultimately charged with two counts of criminal threat. “Threats of any nature are taken seriously by the Hutchinson Police Department and Hutchinson High School. Regardless of whether a post is intended as a joke, it is unlawful to cause others, particularly students, to fear for their safety,” the statement added. Similarly, in Worth county, Georgia , two students at Worth county high school are facing charges after the school district said they participated in the viral social media hoax. Both students involved are being charged, and will also face disciplinary action, school officials say. Due to the potential threats caused by the trend, some school communities have also increased their police presence as a precautionary measure. In a statement released by the Grand Junction police department in Colorado , it said that it increased its presence at West middle school and Grand Junction high school “out of an abundance of caution” after the circulation of a Cat in the Hat post. The post led to the arrest of a 14-year old student. As the trend continues to circulate, law enforcement authorities are urging students to report any safety concerns to a trusted adult, school administrator or law enforcement official rather than reposting or sharing the content. https://www.politico.eu/article/marco-ru.text: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the country had not changed its policy on sharing early warnings of Russian missile attacks with Ukraine and that the Pentagon was not deliberately withholding air defense missiles. "There's nothing being deliberately denied to Ukraine," Rubio said during a visit to India Tuesday, calling reports that the U.S. was not giving Ukraine early warning of Russian ballistic missile attacks "outrageous." "Everything they've been doing with Ukraine remains the same," he said of U.S. Department of Defense policy. "That has not changed. Nothing has changed." Advertisement Advertisement Rubio's comments come as Russia escalates its attacks and Washington moves toward positions more favorable to Moscow, raising European concerns that the U.S. is not a dependable source of support for Ukraine. Rubio was speaking shortly after the EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas accused Washington of trying to force Ukraine to surrender to Russia. "American negotiators have been trying to push Ukraine into surrender for already almost two years," she told the European Parliament on Tuesday morning. On military equipment, Rubio said Ukraine's urgent appeals for more interceptors for Patriot air defense systems had to be balanced against U.S. needs — which are trying to restock thanks to the war against Iran— as well as the demands of other allies. "I know one of the things that President Zelenskyy has been talking about is that he's been trying to buy interceptors. And I understand. So does every other country in the world," Rubio said. "I also talked to Saudi Arabia today. They'd like interceptors. Israel would like interceptors. We would like interceptors. Every country in the world would like interceptors." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday accused the U.S. of holding back on sending air-defense missiles paid for by allies under the NATO-led Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List program. “Unfortunately, the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles that our partners have already paid for through the program PURL,” Zelenskyy said during a video briefing to U.S. lawmakers. Advertisement Advertisement Zelenskyy also said that the U.S. is not always alerting Ukrainian authorities about incoming Russian ballistic missiles; such attacks have become more frequent and are killing people across Ukrainian cities. "Unfortunately, we did not receive an early warning from our partners about the first wave of the Russian ballistic missile attack last night. And we are still facing speed restrictions on Starlink and Starshield services in various sectors of the front. The U.S. side has not provided Ukraine with any explanations regarding either of these two issues," Zelenskyy said in the Monday call . U.S. early warning "always worked and then suddenly it malfunctioned. Nobody in Ukraine believes in this,” an official familiar with the matter told POLITICO on condition of anonymity. “Americans first said it happened because of weather conditions, then it was a software malfunction, then something else … They do not provide an official explanation.” However, Rubio said the U.S. was looking into why Ukraine had problems with information about Russian missiles on Oct. 13 and 18, saying, "perhaps it was an internal issue in terms of them being able to take the information that was being provided and systemize it and react to it." "I think the important takeaway for you is that there has not been some deliberate political directive to go out and harm Ukraine," Rubio said. Ukraine is also complaining that Elon Musk's Starlink has throttled back speeds on its internet connections in Ukraine, making it difficult to intercept Russian drones. Advertisement Advertisement Zelenskyy said Tuesday that he had raised the issues with Rubio. "I am grateful for his willingness to help and his clear position. First, it's about interceptors against ballistic missiles, which are needed to protect lives. Second, it's about early warning of Russian ballistic missile attacks, which is vital. Third, it's about the situation around Starlink/Starshield, which needs to be restored," he said in a social media post. The growing frictions with the U.S. come as President Donald Trump ramps up pressure on Kyiv to stop hitting Russian oil refineries and to reach a peace deal with Moscow. “Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine ... They have not been doing that much,” Trump told reporters on Monday. Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff traveled to Norway on Tuesday for a new round of talks on ending Russia's war against Ukraine. U.N. Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine said that 328 civilians were killed and more than 2,000 wounded across Ukraine last month, an 85% increase from September 2025. The U.N. said that the first two weeks of October were among the deadliest for civilians in years, driven by intensified missile and drone strikes. This story has been updated.
